one_month_reasoning: Events in the window: (1) Micron reports FQ4 2026 after the close today, Sep 30 (consensus ~$51B revenue, $31.61 EPS; the FY27 capex figure, which it earlier framed as 'above the mid-$40 billion range', is the memory-WFE read-through that trades on Oct 1). The bar is high, so I treat it as symmetric. (2) ASML and TSMC Q3 reports in mid-October, with 2027 capacity and capex commentary. (3) Lam's Sep-quarter report, estimated Oct 21-22: Lam has not announced a date, but it reported the Sep-2025 quarter on Oct 22, 2025. The guide of $8.1B / $2.15 was above consensus, and AMAT, ASML and TSMC read-throughs point to a beat and a solid December guide. (4) Samsung and SK hynix Q3 results in late October. Corrected price history: the $438.50 high was June 30, and the fall to ~$252 came in July before earnings. In September the stock traded ~$290 -> $320 -> $269 (Sep 16-17 closes, after the Sep 14 AI 'pacing' call by Anthropic's CEO, which OpenAI and xAI leaders echoed) -> $324. So the stock is not sitting after a one-month collapse. It has retraced a sharp AI-sentiment shock by ~20% in two weeks, and short-horizon reversal and momentum roughly cancel. I centre the distribution near $326 (a small positive tilt for the likely beat) with monthly sigma ~18%, slightly wider than round 1 because realized vol since August is ~55-70% and the stock has had several 6-14% single-day moves since July. Tails are fat because another AI-capex headline could repeat the Sep 14 move.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Sept 2027 of ~$12.0 x 27x = $324, weight 0.6) and FCF yield (CY2027 FCF/share ~$8.55 at a 2.75% yield, plus ~$1/share net cash = $312, weight 0.4) = ~$319, marginally below spot. The EPS base is now anchored on S&P Global FY28 consensus of ~$11.74 and SEMI's independent July 2026 WFE path (+21.8% in 2027, +14.1% in 2028). The multiple steps down from today's ~34x FY27 because by Sept 2027 the market will be pricing a mature-cycle year.

inputs_detail.derivation: S&P Global via StockAnalysis. It replaces my stale Aug snapshot of $9.32.
S&P Global 'next year'. Erste's FY28 is $11.68 (source 15).

SEMI's July 2026 mid-year forecast is the independent anchor: $143.9B in 2026 x 1.218 = ~$175B in 2027, then ~$200B in 2028. Sell-side copies (JPM ~$205B, source 12) run higher. Customer capex supports the upper half: TSMC 2027 at $75-85B, memory big-3 at ~$146B, Micron FY27 above mid-$40Bs. I take ~$180B, which is lower than my round-1 $190B.

The NTM window runs one quarter later than FY28 (consensus $11.74). With SEMI's +14% WFE in 2028, rolling forward a quarter adds ~3-4%, which gives ~$12.1. I trim this to $12.0 for China-curb and supply-constraint risk (sources 13, 14).

Today the stock trades at ~34x FY27 ($324/$9.51) and ~27.6x FY28. By Sept 2027 the market will look through a year whose growth is decelerating (SEMI 2028 +14% vs +22% in 2027). The Sep 14 AI-pacing shock (-18% in three days) shows how fragile the premium is. So I hold 27x on NTM: above semicap's historical high-teens to low-20s range because customers describe tightness beyond 2027 (sources 20, 9), but below today's level.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: CY2027 revenue ~$38B x 28% FCF margin / 1.245B shares = ~$8.55 FCF/share at a 2.75% yield (= $311) + ~$1/share net cash

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 (Jul-26 to Jun-27) consensus revenue is $34.9B (source 19). Moving the window forward two quarters, while WFE grows ~22% in 2027 (SEMI), gives ~$38B, or ~21% of the ~$180B WFE assumed. That is consistent with the share gains management describes.
Operating margin guide is 39.5%. After ~15% tax, capex and working-capital build during a ramp, FCF runs ~28% of revenue.
1.256B diluted in the June quarter, less modest buybacks.
$5.58B cash less ~$4.5B debt, per the Q4 FY26 release.

This matches the ~27x earnings multiple after adjusting for FCF conversion below 100% during the ramp. It is a little higher than round 1's 2.5%, reflecting the mature-cycle framing that peers AMAT and ASML also face.

bear.story: AI-capex doubts (a repeat of the Sep 14 'pacing' shock that turns into actual hyperscaler pauses) spread to fab plans. Memory prices roll over in H1 2027 as ~$146B of big-3 memory capex adds supply, customers push out tools, and the June-2026 FDPR rule and follow-on China curbs bite. The market then prices a 2028 WFE decline, against SEMI's +14%. EPS is ~$9.5 on trough-ish NTM at ~20.5x. Weight trimmed from 25% because every current independent forecast (SEMI July 2026) shows WFE growth in both 2027 and 2028.

base.story: CY27 WFE grows ~20-25% to ~$175-190B (SEMI ~$175B), led by TSMC N2/A16, DRAM/HBM and NAND layer migration, where Lam's etch/dep share is highest. Lam earns ~$12 NTM (in line with the FY28 consensus of $11.74, rolled forward), but the multiple compresses to ~28x as growth decelerates into 2028.

bull.story: Memory stays supply-constrained beyond 2027 (Micron, SK hynix) and TSMC capex of $85B+ pushes CY27 WFE past $200B with a strong 2028. Lam reaches high-30s SAM share, and NAND greenfield plus upgrades accelerate. EPS runs ~$14 and the stock re-rates past its $438.50 June high at ~35x.

thesis_break_reason: $215 is ~-34%, ~18x FY28 consensus ($11.74) and ~23x FY27 ($9.51). It is well below the July 29 pre-earnings close (~$252) and the Sep 16-17 closes (~$269), the two recent sentiment-driven lows. At that price the market would be pricing an outright 2027-28 WFE decline, against SEMI's +21.8% and +14.1%: a memory-capex cut, a TSMC capex reset, AI build-out pauses turning into order push-outs, or a major new China rule. That goes beyond the July and September sentiment swings.

key_uncertainties: The multiple the market pays in Sept 2027 for decelerating growth (2028 WFE +14% vs +22% in 2027, per SEMI). This is the main swing factor, since the EPS path is broadly agreed
Whether AI capex stays durable. The Sep 14 AI-lab 'pacing' call showed that sentiment alone can move the stock ~18% in three days
Memory overbuild risk: big-3 capex ~$146B in 2027, Micron FY27 above mid-$40Bs
China at 26% of revenue (down from 43%): the June-2026 FDPR rule, the Hua Hong halt and a possible MATCH Act floor vote
Supply delivery: cleanroom, lead-time and labour constraints could shift revenue between years
reasoning: Round 2 revision. The supervisor fact-check fixed four things in my round-1 file, and I verified them. (a) FY27 consensus is $9.51 and FY28 ~$11.74 (S&P Global via StockAnalysis), not the $9.32 Aug snapshot. (b) SEMI's July 14, 2026 mid-year forecast, now read directly via Semiconductor Digest, has 2026 WFE at $143.9B (+23.1%), 2027 at +21.8% (~$175B) and 2028 at ~$200B (+14.1%). This is the independent anchor I lacked; it sits just below the sell-side's $180-205B, so I cut my CY27 WFE to ~$180B. (c) I misdated the drawdown. The $438.50 high was June 30 and the ~$252 low came in late July. September's swing ($320 -> $269 -> $324) was driven by the Sep 14 Anthropic 'pacing' call (24/7 Wall St, verified) and the Sep 10 yield move. The stock has since fully retraced, which lowers the weight on a 'broken momentum' story. (d) Micron's FY27 capex 'above the mid-$40 billion range' and 'tightness beyond 2027' are confirmed from its Q3 call transcript. Its FQ4 print lands after today's close. Industry read is unchanged: customers (TSMC, Micron, SK hynix), peers (AMAT) and suppliers (ASML) all point to a stronger 2027. Valuation: NTM EPS ~$12.0 x 27x = $324, and FCF ~$8.55/share at a 2.75% yield plus net cash = $312. Blended fair value is $319, marginally below spot. The higher EPS base is offset by a mature-cycle multiple. I disagree mildly with the supervisor's 26.5x/$310. The customers' and SEMI's visibility into 2028 (+14% growth, not digestion) argues against compressing below ~27x NTM a year before any forecast peak, so I stay a little higher. Distribution: median ~$338-340, a lognormal mixture with effective sigma ~0.50 (fat tails for AI-sentiment shocks and cycle turns). The bear weight is trimmed to 23% because no current forecast shows a 2027-28 WFE decline. That lifts mid-ladder probabilities ~1-1.5 pts vs round 1. Research this round was ~7 queries/fetches; sec.gov returned an empty file for Micron's 8-K, so Micron capex is from its call transcript.
